episode_title: Collaboration Unscripted: What we are learning along the way
question: How does collaborative coaching differ from typical team coaching in addressing multi-organization or multi-team dynamics?
transcript_excerpt: Collaborative coaching is different than typical team coaching because now you are looking at teams of teams, different organizations. Understanding words and what they mean becomes important because how one team collaborates could be very different than how another team collaborates. Creating space for that understanding becomes valuable when bringing multiple teams together who assume they will just figure it out and work together.

episode_title: Collaboration Unscripted: What we are learning along the way
question: What happens when both sides of a conflict want to be right in organizational or team settings?
transcript_excerpt: When both sides of the table everyone wants to be right, it is very hard to meet in the middle and come to consensus or agreement. This pattern often emerges particularly when things are charged and emotions are in the room. The challenge is understanding what collaboration actually means before teams get dug in so hard that it becomes much harder to unwind.

episode_title: Collaboration Unscripted: What we are learning along the way
question: Why is addressing small relational tensions early critical to team and project success?
transcript_excerpt: Small relational things are often the things that get in the way of the overall success of a team and project. Teams tend to avoid those little relational things, but they become really big mountains or big stories. If you address that small thing 18 months ago instead of avoiding it, you would be in a completely different place today versus letting those tensions build.

episode_title: Collaboration Unscripted: What we are learning along the way
question: What role does a third-party coach play in helping multi-organization or cross-team collaboration succeed?
transcript_excerpt: Having a coach present helps people understand when they are not understanding the other person or team, and allows stopping the conversation to ensure alignment. A third party can help set the table for the right language and understanding. People have said they would not have gotten as far without having coaches there to help navigate conversations where both sides are saying the same thing but cannot hear each other.

episode_title: Collaboration Unscripted: What we are learning along the way
question: How does reframing conversation around shared outcomes help teams move past being stuck on being right?
transcript_excerpt: When teams can reground in the why or the outcome they are looking for, it can help people step back and let go of the stuff they are hanging on to. Whether it is a patient and family in healthcare or a project outcome, surfacing the outcome in a way that helps people shed some of the things they are stuck on can be really helpful in shifting from individual rightness to collective purpose.
